text.title: Mallard
text.menu_sub: Paddle on the lakes and fly between shores.
text.menu_wild: Foxes catch you on the ground.
text.intro: Steer to paddle. Hold Fly to take off from the water.
text.hungry: Look for water plants and small water animals.
text.no_food: No food nearby. Explore the shallow water.
text.chased: A predator! Swim away or take flight.
text.about_looks: A brown female mallard, with a broad bill and a blue wing patch.
text.about_food: Water plants, seeds and small invertebrates.
text.about_home: Lakes, ponds and sheltered shores. Nests hidden on the ground.
text.about_winter: Most migrate to open water farther south.
text.about_young: The mother leads her ducklings to water. They find their own food.
text.about_fact: A mallard can feed by tipping its head underwater and leaving its tail pointing up.

year.shelter: Sheltered shores; ground nest hidden in vegetation. Current game uses vegetation shelter.
year.young: Female lays 5–12 eggs in April–May and leads the ducklings.

food.spring: Water plants, seeds and aquatic invertebrates.
food.summer: Water plants, seeds and aquatic invertebrates.
food.autumn: Water plants, seeds and aquatic invertebrates.
food.winter: Water plants, seeds and aquatic invertebrates.

year.notes: Female plumage. First version has surface paddling and flight; no duckling family yet.
